soft_issues: Table 3 lists 720 observations while Table 4 and the results text use 712. Both figures are kept as the extract states them.
The 20 km infection-risk radius is cited from Aldrin epidemiology, not estimated in this paper.

claim_checks.claim: Highest infection risk is described as within a 20 km radius, citing Aldrin work. The paper estimates a translog cost function with two proximity indicators on a 119-firm panel.
claim_checks.extract_quote: the highest risk for negative spatial biological externalities from other farms related to fish diseases and salmon lice seems to be within 20 km radius of the farm.

claim_checks.claim: Reported elasticities use firm fixed-effect models (712 observations). Table 3 lists 720 observations for the same 119 firms.
claim_checks.note: Table 3 says 720 observations. Soft inconsistency, not a fabricated number.

claim_checks.claim: Doubling mean nearest-farm distance is associated with an 8.7 percent cost reduction. Doubling farms within 20 km is associated with an 18.3 percent cost increase.
claim_checks.extract_quote: For the sample mean firm, doubling the mean distance to the nearest farm is associated with an 8.7% reduction in production costs.

claim_checks.claim: Sample means are about 5.08 km to the nearest farm and about 9.78 farms within 20 km. The October 2018 map shows 620 sites.
claim_checks.extract_quote: Figure 2 displays the distribution of 620 salmon aquaculture production sites along the coastline of Norway, as recorded in the October 2018 aquaculture registry.

claim_checks.claim: Industry indexes 2012-2020: farms up 16 percent, production up 25 percent, fish loss up 35 percent, lice prevalence down about 30 percent, treatments up 98 percent, inflation-adjusted costs up 57 percent.
claim_checks.extract_quote: the number of active farms and production has increased by 16 and 25% during the time period 2012–2020.
claim_checks.note: Loss, lice, treatments and cost figures are in the same industry-index paragraphs.

claim_checks.claim: Annual technical change about 3.2 percent (A) and 3.1 percent (B), interpreted as costs shifting upwards. Proximity-bias terms are not statistically significant.
claim_checks.extract_quote: The derived estimate of annual technical change (TC) is around 3.2% in Model A and 3.1% in Model B. Hence, both models imply that costs shifted upwards

claim_checks.claim: Food Safety Authority minimum distances are 5 km for new facilities, and 2.5 km for facilities up to 3,600 tons MTB (5 km above that).
claim_checks.extract_quote: presently stands at 5 km for new facilities. In 2018, facilities with a Maximum Allowed Biomass (MTB) of up to 3,600 tons were required to maintain a minimum distance of 2.5 km
claim_checks.note: The authors also state a noticeable lack of rules on site distribution.

claim_checks.claim: Policy implication: avoid further increased spatial density of open-cage farms. Tools named include location-structure regulation, biosecurity, emission quotas, and innovation policy. Qviller et al. 2024 is cited.
claim_checks.extract_quote: they imply that one should avoid further increased spatial density of open cage farms.
claim_checks.note: Qviller citation is in the same concluding section.

evidence_direction_note: supports_effect is defensible. The paper claims and estimates that greater proximity is associated with higher production cost, treated as spatial biological externalities.
priority_questions_note: A5 only (density, productivity, biosecurity). A3 not tagged. Wild-salmon licence-to-grow text is a concluding implication, not a coexistence study.
coi_note: A disclosure statement is present. coi_declared set to yes. Funding is RCN 320612, 328724 and 353039. Tveterås lists Blue Planet board, SalmonTracking, and consultancy.
extract_coverage: Walked the full extracted.md: abstract, introduction, spatial-externality review, 620-site maps, Table 1, regulation and 2012-2020 industry indexes, methods (translog, 119 firms), results (elasticities, technical change), conclusion, notes, acknowledgements, disclosure, and references.
